symptom: alter workflow: `drop X outcome 'V'` / `drop X outcome <enum value>` dropped the first of two outcomes sharing that value; `drop X boundary event` could not say which of several events, so under mdl 1 it was refused with no way to drop the second; check-time guards went silent on a reference the mutator resolved by name, because resolveStoredActivity pooled a jump captioned with its target's name with the target itself
cause: Both mutators' drop loops stopped at the first match and never counted; the boundary-event op carried no address at all; the executor's resolveStoredActivity copied findActivityByCaption but not its preferNameMatches narrowing
fix: A value that matches more than one outcome is refused as ambiguous, nothing written, in both mutators; `boundary event N` (1-based, describe order) addresses one event, out of range refused at exec before the mutator; resolveStoredActivity prefers Name matches without @N
insight: A check-time resolver that mirrors a mutator must mirror every narrowing step, or the check silently abstains (it returns nil on ambiguity by design) exactly where exec acts; test the resolver on the jump-caption shape directly. A drop loop with `!found` guards is the tell for a first-match guess: count matches, then decide
